courses.title: Cybersecurity Foundations: Protect the Digital World
courses.description: Recognise common attacks, protect accounts and devices, and build safer digital habits from the ground up.
courses.longDescription: A beginner-friendly micro-course that explains cyber risk through short visual lessons, familiar examples, and practical safety checks for everyday university life.
courses.imageAlt: A bright blue shield and keyhole connected to an abstract circuit network

instructor.name: NEST Learning Team
instructor.bio: Developed as a collaborative NEST micro-course for students beginning their journey into digital safety and ethical cyber awareness.

outcomes: Explain why cybersecurity matters to individuals and organisations
Recognise malware, phishing, social engineering, and password attacks
Apply stronger authentication, browsing, Wi-Fi, update, and backup practices
Describe core network-security controls including firewalls, encryption, HTTPS, and VPNs

modules.title: Introduction to Cybersecurity
modules.description: Build the vocabulary needed to discuss threats, protection, and digital trust.

lessons.title: What is Cybersecurity?
lessons.description: Understand how people, processes, and technology protect systems and information.
lessons.learningObjective: Explain the role and meaning of “Cybersecurity” and connect it to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: List three digital assets you use at university and one protection for each.
lessons.recap: Understand how people, processes, and technology protect systems and information.

lessons.title: Why Cybersecurity Matters
lessons.description: Connect security incidents to privacy, finances, learning, reputation, and organisational continuity.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Why Cybersecurity Matters” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Trace the possible impact of a compromised university account.
lessons.recap: Connect security incidents to privacy, finances, learning, reputation, and organisational continuity.

lessons.title: Types of Hackers
lessons.description: Compare white-hat, black-hat, and grey-hat activity through permission and intent.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Types of Hackers” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Classify three short scenarios by intent and authorisation.
lessons.recap: Compare white-hat, black-hat, and grey-hat activity through permission and intent.

lessons.title: Common Cyber Threats Overview
lessons.description: Survey the attacks beginners are most likely to encounter online.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Common Cyber Threats Overview” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Match each threat to the warning sign that best reveals it.
lessons.recap: Survey the attacks beginners are most likely to encounter online.

lessons.title: The CIA Triad
lessons.description: Use confidentiality, integrity, and availability to describe what security protects.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “The CIA Triad” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Apply the CIA triad to a student records system.
lessons.recap: Use confidentiality, integrity, and availability to describe what security protects.

modules.title: Common Attacks
modules.description: Recognise how common attacks work and the signals that help expose them.

lessons.learningObjective: Explain the role and meaning of “Malware” and connect it to a familiar technology scenario.

lessons.recap: Learn how malicious software disrupts, spies on, damages, or controls devices.

lessons.title: Virus vs Worm vs Trojan

lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Virus vs Worm vs Trojan” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.

lessons.title: What is Phishing?

lessons.learningObjective: Explain the role and meaning of “Phishing” and connect it to a familiar technology scenario.

lessons.recap: Spot messages designed to steal information or pressure you into an unsafe action.

lessons.title: Password Attacks

lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Password Attacks” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.

lessons.title: Man-in-the-Middle Attacks

lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Man-in-the-Middle Attacks” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Draw the normal path and intercepted path of a web request.
lessons.recap: See how an attacker can intercept communication between two trusted endpoints.

lessons.title: Social Engineering Basics
lessons.description: Recognise manipulation that targets human trust rather than technical weaknesses.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Social Engineering Basics” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Rewrite a pressured response into a calm verification step.
lessons.recap: Recognise manipulation that targets human trust rather than technical weaknesses.

lessons.title: Ransomware Explained
lessons.description: Understand how ransomware blocks access to data and why recovery planning matters.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Ransomware Explained” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Choose the safest first responses to a ransomware warning.
lessons.recap: Understand how ransomware blocks access to data and why recovery planning matters.

lessons.title: Zero-Day Attacks

lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Zero-Day Attacks” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Explain why updates and multiple safeguards still matter when no patch exists.

modules.title: Authentication & Password Security
modules.description: Build safer account habits and understand how systems verify identity.

lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “What Makes a Strong Password” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.

lessons.recap: Create memorable passphrases that resist guessing and automated attacks.

lessons.title: Password Managers

lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Password Managers” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Draft a checklist for choosing and setting up a password manager.
lessons.recap: Use an encrypted vault to create and store unique credentials.

modules.title: Network Security Basics
modules.description: Meet the network concepts and controls that protect data in transit.

lessons.title: What is a Network?
lessons.description: See how connected devices exchange data and share services.
lessons.learningObjective: Explain the role and meaning of “a Network” and connect it to a familiar technology scenario.

lessons.title: VPN Basics

lessons.recap: Understand how a VPN creates an encrypted tunnel to a trusted service.

modules.title: Safe Practices
modules.description: Turn cybersecurity knowledge into a repeatable personal protection routine.

lessons.title: Safe Browsing Tips

lessons.activity: Design a backup plan for important coursework.

courses.title: Networking Essentials: How Digital Connections Work
courses.description: Follow data across devices, addresses, protocols, and services, then apply the ideas to a practical small network.
courses.longDescription: A visual beginner micro-course that turns networking terminology into one connected story—from the first local link to internet services and practical troubleshooting.
courses.imageAlt: A bright orange wireless router linking a balanced network of connected nodes

instructor.name: NEST Learning Team
instructor.bio: Developed as a collaborative NEST micro-course to make the systems behind everyday connectivity visible and approachable.

outcomes: Identify common network types, devices, addresses, and protocols
Explain how packets travel across local networks and the internet
Describe core safety controls including firewalls, VPNs, and encryption

lessons.title: What is a Microcontroller?
lessons.description: Understand the compact computer that coordinates inputs, processing, memory, and outputs.
lessons.learningObjective: Explain the role and meaning of “a Microcontroller” and connect it to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Identify where a microcontroller fits in the sense-think-act loop.
lessons.recap: Understand the compact computer that coordinates inputs, processing, memory, and outputs.

lessons.title: Arduino Overview
lessons.description: Meet the Arduino board, programming workflow, and ATmega328P-based control system.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Arduino Overview” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Label the main sections of an Arduino Uno-style board.
lessons.recap: Meet the Arduino board, programming workflow, and ATmega328P-based control system.

lessons.title: Digital Input & Output
lessons.description: Read two-state inputs and control two-state outputs with digital pins.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Digital Input & Output” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Plan the logic for a button controlling an LED.
lessons.recap: Read two-state inputs and control two-state outputs with digital pins.

lessons.title: Blink LED Concept
lessons.description: Follow the sequence of switching an output on, waiting, and switching it off.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Blink LED Concept” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Arrange the steps of a blink sequence in the correct order.
lessons.recap: Follow the sequence of switching an output on, waiting, and switching it off.

lessons.title: Push Button Input
lessons.description: Use a button as a digital input and understand stable pull-up or pull-down states.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Push Button Input” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Predict input readings when a wired button is pressed and released.
lessons.recap: Use a button as a digital input and understand stable pull-up or pull-down states.

lessons.title: PWM Basics
lessons.description: Control how long a digital output stays on during each rapid pulse cycle by changing its duty cycle.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “PWM Basics” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Compare LED brightness at 25%, 50%, and 90% duty cycles.
lessons.recap: Control how long a digital output stays on during each rapid pulse cycle by changing its duty cycle.

lessons.title: Servo Motor Basics
lessons.description: Command a servo to move toward a controlled angular position.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Servo Motor Basics” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Choose suitable servo positions for a small robot arm.
lessons.recap: Command a servo to move toward a controlled angular position.

lessons.title: Interfacing Sensors
lessons.description: Connect power, ground, and signal lines, then interpret a sensor's output.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Interfacing Sensors” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Create a connection checklist for a three-pin sensor.
lessons.recap: Connect power, ground, and signal lines, then interpret a sensor's output.

modules.title: Motion & Control
modules.description: Turn controller decisions into reliable movement and improve behaviour with feedback.

lessons.title: Types of Motors
lessons.description: Compare DC, servo, and stepper motors by speed, position, and control needs.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Types of Motors” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Select a motor for wheels, steering, and precise rotation.
lessons.recap: Compare DC, servo, and stepper motors by speed, position, and control needs.

lessons.title: How Motors Work
lessons.description: See how electrical energy and magnetic forces produce rotational movement.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “How Motors Work” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Explain motor rotation using a simple magnetic interaction diagram.
lessons.recap: See how electrical energy and magnetic forces produce rotational movement.

lessons.title: Motor Driver Concept
lessons.description: Use a driver circuit to provide motor current and direction safely beyond a controller pin.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Motor Driver Concept” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Place a motor driver correctly between a microcontroller and motors.
lessons.recap: Use a driver circuit to provide motor current and direction safely beyond a controller pin.

lessons.title: What is Feedback?
lessons.description: Measure results and use them to correct or stabilise a robot's behaviour.
lessons.learningObjective: Explain the role and meaning of “Feedback” and connect it to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Describe feedback for maintaining a robot's speed.
lessons.recap: Measure results and use them to correct or stabilise a robot's behaviour.

lessons.title: Open Loop vs Closed Loop
lessons.description: Compare commands without measurement to control that responds to measured output.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Open Loop vs Closed Loop” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Classify a timer-based turn and sensor-corrected turn.
lessons.recap: Compare commands without measurement to control that responds to measured output.

lessons.title: Line Following Robot Concept
lessons.description: Combine reflectance sensors, decisions, and motor adjustments to follow a path.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Line Following Robot Concept” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Build a decision table for left, centre, and right sensor readings.
lessons.recap: Combine reflectance sensors, decisions, and motor adjustments to follow a path.

modules.title: Smart Robotics & IoT
modules.description: Connect robots to wireless services, cloud data, and emerging intelligent applications.

lessons.title: What is IoT in Robotics?
lessons.description: Understand how connected robots exchange data with applications, services, and other devices.
lessons.learningObjective: Explain the role and meaning of “IoT in Robotics” and connect it to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Map the data flow for a remotely monitored robot.
lessons.recap: Understand how connected robots exchange data with applications, services, and other devices.

lessons.title: Wireless Communication Basics
lessons.description: Compare common short- and medium-range ways for robots to communicate without cables.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Wireless Communication Basics” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Choose a wireless option for control, telemetry, and cloud access.
lessons.recap: Compare common short- and medium-range ways for robots to communicate without cables.

lessons.title: Robot + Sensors + Cloud
lessons.description: Follow sensor readings from the robot to storage, analysis, and a user dashboard.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Robot + Sensors + Cloud” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Diagram a temperature-monitoring robot and its cloud data path.
lessons.recap: Follow sensor readings from the robot to storage, analysis, and a user dashboard.

lessons.title: Smart Home Robot Example
lessons.description: Combine sensing, movement, connectivity, and user interaction in one household scenario.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Smart Home Robot Example” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Define the sense-think-act loop for a home assistance task.
lessons.recap: Combine sensing, movement, connectivity, and user interaction in one household scenario.

lessons.title: Future of Robotics
lessons.description: Explore collaborative robots, autonomy, responsible design, and new human-robot roles.
lessons.learningObjective: Describe the key ideas behind “Future of Robotics” and apply them to a familiar technology scenario.
lessons.activity: Propose one beneficial future robot and one design responsibility.
lessons.recap: Explore collaborative robots, autonomy, responsible design, and new human-robot roles.
